title: My Bedtime Checklist
text:
Every night I follow my bedtime checklist. Mom wrote it on a big piece of paper and taped it to my door.

First, I take a warm bath with my rubber duck and {number} {plural noun}. Then I put on my pajamas. Tonight I am wearing the ones with little {plural noun} all over them. They are very {adjective}.

Next, I brush my teeth for two whole minutes. Dad says to brush {adverb}, the way a {animal} would. After that, I pick one book for story time. My favorite book is about a {noun} who learns how to {verb}.

Last, I get a sip of water and a {adjective} hug from everybody in the house, even the cat. I turn on my night light, which is shaped like a {noun}. Then I close my eyes and dream about {verb ending in ing}.

title: My Dream Report for Tuesday Night
text:
Dream report by Leo, age six. I went to sleep at eight o'clock and woke up at seven. Here is what I dreamed.

In my dream, I was the captain of a big boat made of {plural noun}. My first mate was a {adjective} {animal} named Mr. Wiggles. We sailed {adverb} across a sea of warm {food}. Every time a wave came, Mr. Wiggles shouted {exclamation} and did a little dance.

Then we landed on an island where everybody was {verb ending in ing}. The mayor of the island gave me a golden {noun} and asked me to {verb} at the island party. I was very good at it.

Right before I woke up, my dog jumped on my bed, and the whole island {past tense verb}. I told Mom about it at breakfast. She said it sounded like a {adjective} dream.

title: How to Sing a Lullaby to a Baby Brother
text:
My baby brother Max does not like to go to sleep. Mom taught me how to sing him a lullaby, and now I am an expert. Here are my instructions.

First, make sure the room is dark and quiet. Turn on the fan and give Max his favorite {noun} to hold. He likes to chew on it until it is {adjective}.

Next, sit in the rocking chair and rock {adverb}. Start singing very softly. The best lullaby goes like this: Hush little baby, don't you {verb}, Mama's going to buy you {number} {plural noun}. If his eyes are still open, add a verse about a sleepy {animal} who is {verb ending in ing} on a cloud.

When Max finally closes his eyes, tiptoe out of the room. Do not {verb}, do not sneeze, and do not step on the {adjective} floorboard by the door. If he wakes up, you have to start over and sing about {plural noun}.

title: Bedtime Roll Call for My Stuffed Animals
text:
Before I go to sleep, I take roll call so all my stuffed animals are in bed with me. I have {number} stuffed friends, so it takes a while.

First is Bear. Bear sleeps on my pillow because he is the most {adjective}. Next is Bunny, who always wants to {verb} before she can fall asleep. Then comes Duck, who is wearing a tiny {noun} on his head tonight. I do not know where he got it.

The newest one is a stuffed {animal} that Grandma gave me. Her name is Princess {silly word}. She is a little shy, so I tuck her in {adverb} and tell her about my day. Today I told her that we {past tense verb} at recess.

When everyone is here, I say goodnight to each one. Then Mom checks under my blanket. Last night she found three {plural noun} and a sock in there. She said they could stay, as long as they do not {verb} all night.

title: A Letter to the Moon
text:
Dear Moon, I can see you from my bedroom window every night. You are round and {adjective}, and you look like a big {noun} in the sky. I hope you are doing well up there.

I have some questions for you. Do you ever get tired of staying up all night? Do the stars help you {verb} when you are bored? My teacher, Ms. Bell, says you are made of rock, but my brother says you are made of {food}. Please tell me who is right.

Tonight I am going to leave a little gift on my windowsill for you. It is a drawing of {number} {plural noun} having a picnic. I colored it very {adverb}.

Well, Mom says it is time to put away my {plural noun} and turn off the light. I will wave to you before I close my eyes. If you see me {verb ending in ing} in my sleep, please wave back. Love, Ruby

title: Tonight's Pillow Fort Forecast
text:
Good evening! This is Nora with the weather forecast for the pillow fort in my bedroom. Right now it is cozy and {adjective} inside the fort. There is a light breeze coming from the fan, and a small chance of {plural noun} around midnight.

Later tonight, we expect a big storm of tickles from Dad. When the tickle storm arrives, everyone should hide under the {noun} and giggle {adverb}. After that, the weather will clear up, and it will be time to {verb}.

Tomorrow morning will be sunny, with pancakes and a high of {number} {plural noun}. My cat, Mittens, will be {verb ending in ing} on the windowsill all day, which is normal for this time of year.

That is the forecast. Please bring your favorite blanket and a {adjective} flashlight. Back to you, Mom.

title: Rules for Reading a Bedtime Story
text:
In our house, Dad reads the bedtime story. After many years of practice, he has made some rules.

Rule one: The reader must use a different voice for every character. The dragon gets a deep voice, the princess gets a squeaky voice, and the {noun} gets a voice that sounds like a {adjective} teapot. Rule two: The listener may ask {number} questions and no more. Last night my sister asked why the giant was afraid of {plural noun}. Dad said it was a good question.

Rule three: Nobody is allowed to {verb} during the sad part. Rule four: If the reader falls asleep first, the listener must tap him {adverb} on the {body part} and say wake up, please. Rule five: Every story must end with somebody {verb ending in ing} happily ever after.

Dad says if we follow the rules, he will read the one about the {adjective} pirate who found a treasure chest full of {plural noun}.

title: Grandpa's Sleepover Schedule
text:
I am sleeping over at Grandpa Walt's house tonight. Grandpa made a schedule and stuck it on the fridge with a magnet shaped like a {noun}.

At six o'clock, we eat dinner. Grandpa is making his famous spaghetti with {plural noun} on top. At seven o'clock, we go outside to look at the stars and {verb} in the backyard. Grandpa says the brightest star is called {silly word}.

At eight o'clock, we put on pajamas and have warm milk. Grandpa likes to stir his milk {adverb} with a {adjective} spoon. Then he tells me the story of when he was a boy and {past tense verb} all the way to school.

At nine o'clock, it is lights out. Grandpa checks the windows, gives me a {adjective} goodnight hug, and turns on his radio. He says the only way he can fall asleep is by listening to {verb ending in ing} {plural noun}.

title: Reasons I Need Five More Minutes
text:
Dear Mom and Dad, I know it is bedtime. I have brushed my teeth and put on my pajamas. But I have made a list of very good reasons why I need five more minutes.

Reason one: My goldfish has not said goodnight yet, and she gets {adjective} when I forget. Reason two: I still need to finish my tower of {plural noun}. It is almost as tall as the {noun}.

Reason three: I just remembered that tomorrow is {food} Day at school, and I need to practice. Reason four: I heard the cat {verb ending in ing} in the hallway, and I want to make sure she is okay.

Reason five: I am not even tired. I am wide awake and ready to {verb}. Look how {adverb} I can hop on one foot! If you say yes, I promise to go straight to sleep and dream about {plural noun}. Love, your {adjective} kid, Sam
